entries.title: Protection orders, residence orders and money relief
entries.act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entries.plain_summary: This Act is a civil law that protects women from physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse inside a shared household. A magistrate can pass orders that stop the abuse, protect her right to stay in the house, and require maintenance or compensation.
key_points: The Act covers physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse, including threats and humiliation.
A magistrate can pass a protection order under section 18, a residence order under section 19, monetary relief under section 20 and compensation under section 22.
She can apply herself, or through a Protection Officer, a registered service provider or a lawyer.
A breach of a protection order is itself an offence, so keep a copy of the order safe.

entries.title: Who to contact first under the Domestic Violence Act
entries.act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entries.plain_summary: Every district has Protection Officers whose job is to help a woman file a Domestic Incident Report and reach the magistrate. Registered service providers (shelters, NGOs) and One Stop Centres can also help, usually free of cost.
key_points: A Protection Officer can record a Domestic Incident Report (DIR) and help file the application in court.
One Stop Centres (Sakhi Centres) offer police, medical, legal and shelter support in one place.
She does not need a lawyer to file, but legal aid is free for women through the District Legal Services Authority.
Keep copies of the DIR and any order; they matter if the situation escalates.
